Nobody is going to read forty pages of terms before ordering dinner, and I would never ask you to. But there are three clauses I always read, and you can find them in five minutes with the search function. First, look for the word liable. That clause tells you what the company says it will not pay for. Second, look for dispute or arbitration. That tells you where you will have to go if something goes wrong, and sometimes it is another country. Third, look for share or third parties. That tells you who else receives your data. And remember that finding a clause is not the same as accepting it. If a clause says the company is never responsible for anything, a court may decide that it is void. The contract is important, but it is not the only thing that protects you.

We have updated our terms of service, and we want to explain the most important changes in plain language. Starting next month, if your order arrives more than forty-five minutes late, you may receive a credit for your next order. You are entitled to a full refund only if the order never arrives. We may share some personal data with payment and delivery partners, but we shall not sell your data to advertisers. You may opt out of marketing messages at any time, and you are not required to give us your birthday. Finally, disputes that cannot be solved by our support team shall be resolved by arbitration. If you continue to use the app after thirty days, you consent to these changes. If you do not agree, you may close your account before then.
